chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from his father, and al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala, from Abi al-'Ala, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

One whose recitation in the obligatory prayer is Surah Al-Balad, will be known in this world as one of the virtuous, and will be known in the Hereafter as having a station with Allah, and will be on the Day of Resurrection among the companions of the prophets, the martyrs, and the virtuous.
ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for reciting Surah Al-Balad in obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to emphasize the transformative power of reciting Surah Al-Balad with presence of heart during obligatory prayers, linking it to the oath of Mecca ('this city') found in the Surah itself. The hadith promises worldly recognition as a righteous person and a unique, elevated station with Allah in the Hereafter, culminating in companionship with the prophets, martyrs, and the truthful on the Day of Judgment.
